display.purpose: The clock only. Largest, most glanceable element in the system.

headline.purpose: Big readout numbers: tariffs, consumption, graph values, weather hero temp (uses weight 300 as its one exception).

body.purpose: Media titles, calendar entries, card copy.

label.purpose: Captions, units, the Label pill, calendar timestamps.

motion.name: tap-feedback
motion.purpose: Fast confirm for a direct tap: sidebar tile active-state scale, hover/focus transitions.

motion.name: ambient-state-fade
motion.purpose: Slow, deliberate fade for state that changes on its own or lags a toggle: LightCard background color and brightness-thumb position.

components.name: Card (default)
components.description: Base surface for nearly all content; built-in tap vs. 1000ms long-press handling.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #1e293b; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.9); border-radius: 24px; padding: 16px; overflow: hidden; }

components.name: Card (Neutral variant)
components.description: One tone darker/flatter than the default card; used for secondary stat tiles that should recede behind primary content.
components.css: .ds-card-neutral { background: #171717; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.9); border-radius: 24px; padding: 16px; text-align: center; }

components.name: TileButton (sidebar nav)
components.description: 64×64px section-accent nav pill. Active state drops the vignette and scales to 105%.
components.css: .ds-tile-button { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 64px; height: 64px; margin: 8px; border-radius: 24px; background: #93c5fd; background-image: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(0,0,0,0.1), rgba(0,0,0,0.4)); color: #000; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 0.2s ease, background-image 0.2s ease; } .ds-tile-button:hover { transform: scale(1.03); } .ds-tile-button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #fff; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-tile-button--active { background-image: none; transform: scale(1.05); }

components.name: Label (pill tag)
components.description: Small black pill for section captions and inline chart value callouts.
components.css: .ds-label { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #000; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.9); font-size: 14px; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px 16px; }

components.name: Badge (status dot)
components.description: Plain colored dot conveying state (tariff band) by color alone; absolutely positioned on its host.
components.css: .ds-badge { position: absolute; display: inline-block; min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px; border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-badge--low { background: #16a34a; } .ds-badge--normal { background: #fff; } .ds-badge--high { background: #ef4444; }

components.name: LightCard (toggle tile)
components.description: Signature component: a full card that is also a light toggle. Tap toggles on/off; 1000ms hold opens the detail modal. Background and brightness-thumb position both animate over 1000ms.
components.css: .ds-light-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; min-height: 125px; width: 100%; padding: 16px; border: none; border-radius: 24px; cursor: pointer; font: inherit; text-align: left; transition: background-color 1000ms ease; } .ds-light-card--on { background: #fdba74; color: #000; } .ds-light-card--off { background: #1e293b; color: #fff; } .ds-light-card__label { flex: 1; } .ds-light-card__track { position: relative; height: 16px; width: 100%; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0 8px; } .ds-light-card--on .ds-light-card__track { background: linear-gradient(to right, rgba(255,255,255,0.3), #fff); } .ds-light-card--off .ds-light-card__track { background: rgba(100,116,139,0.2); } .ds-light-card__thumb { position: absolute; top: 50%; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 6px; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); transition: left 1000ms ease; } .ds-light-card--on .ds-light-card__thumb { background: #000; } .ds-light-card--off .ds-light-card__thumb { background: #fff; }

narrative.overview:
The dashboard is a black instrument panel, not a page. color-scheme: dark and a pure black (#000000) canvas sit under everything; surfaces don't compete for attention, they recede into slate/neutral tone-steps until a value or a state needs to say something. Color is a signal, not decoration: the sidebar tiles carry one accent hue each so a room-scale glance tells Home from Energy from Weather from Vacuum; a light tile turns warm orange the instant it's on; the tariff trio (green / muted teal / burnt orange) is the one place hue directly encodes a number. Nothing here is trying to look expensive or branded — it's trying to be legible from the couch and forgiving to a thumb.

Built for a wall-mounted kiosk tablet, touched, not clicked, and read from a few meters away — this is the reason for the oversized numerals (text-8xl clock), the chunky rounded-3xl tiles, and the total absence of small hit targets, hover-only affordances, or dense tabular UI. It is explicitly not a SaaS admin dashboard (no tables, no dense sidebars, no 12px captions) and not a skeuomorphic/glassy smart-home app (no blur, no glass panels, no decorative gradients beyond the two functional ones: weather sky and light-brightness track).
keyCharacteristics: Pure black canvas; depth from tonal layering only, never shadows.
One accent hue per section/state, otherwise monochrome.
Everything sized for a thumb and readable from across the room.
Motion is slow and ambient (1s color/position fades) or a quick confirm (200ms tap feedback) — never decorative.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: A surface gets exactly one reason to have color: its section identity (sidebar tile), its state (light on/off, tariff band), or an error. Never decorate a surface with color it doesn't need to communicate.

rules.name: The No-Alarm-Red Rule
rules.body: Red (#ef4444) is reserved for actual errors and the sidebar's "high tariff" badge. Peak cost itself is burnt orange (#DC6731), not red — a cost signal should read as "pay attention," not "something is broken."

rules.name: The One Weight Does the Talking Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size and weight (600 vs 400), never from a second typeface. If a new surface needs "more emphasis," reach for size or weight before reaching for a new font.

rules.name: The 24px Rhythm Rule
rules.body: gap-6 (24px) is the default spacing between every major block — sidebar-to-content, card-to-card, section-to-section. gap-4 (16px) is the one step down, for internal card content.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Never add a box-shadow to match a "modern card" instinct. If something needs to feel closer to the viewer, lighten its tone or brighten its color — don't lift it.

dos: Do keep the canvas pure black (#000000) and let card surfaces (slate-800/neutral-900/neutral-800) do all the tonal separation.
Do give each dashboard section exactly one accent hue and reuse it consistently for that section's identity (sidebar tile, related badges).
Do use rounded-3xl (24px) for any new primary surface (card, tile) so it matches the system's signature shape.
Do size interactive targets for a thumb, viewed from a few meters — err large, not compact.
Do use slow (~1000ms) transitions for ambient state changes (color, position) and fast (~200ms) transitions for direct tap feedback (scale).
donts: Don't add box-shadow anywhere — depth comes from tone, not elevation.
Don't introduce a second typeface or lean on italics/letter-spacing for hierarchy — Poppins weight and size already do that job.
Don't use red for anything other than genuine errors or the "high tariff" badge; peak-cost states use burnt orange (#DC6731), not alarm colors.
Don't add responsive breakpoints or a fluid layout without confirming the target device changed — this ships to one fixed kiosk viewport.
Don't promote a one-off functional color (like a single weather-icon hue) into a system-wide token; keep categorical lookups local to the component that needs them.
